correctness.rationale: The pairwise chord bound \(\le2t\) forces any sequence of radius-t triangles with t tending to zero toward one common genuine polygon corner, since a triple on one edge is collinear. Distances between the two incident rays bound all local ray coordinates. Substitution of two ray distances as multiples of the third has Jacobian \(c^2\) and gives the exact corner-volume integral \(8t^3(1+\cos\theta)^2/(3\sin\theta)\). Exactly six ordered label/orientation choices contribute each corner, proving the unconditional probability and the exact coefficient. The exterior-angle score has strictly positive second derivative, so Jensen gives the equality class. Direct substitution gives the regular polygon value. Numerical script checks are supplementary, not certificates of infinite correctness.

originality.rationale: Actual record and primary literature searches found random triangle laws with different sample spaces (circle points, triangle side-length triples, or area-uniform smooth-body points), and a two-point boundary-distance law; their conclusions do not imply an exact three-point boundary circumradius coefficient depending on polygon angles. Unindexed equivalent results remain possible.

value.rationale: The theorem gives an exact local law for the circumradius of three iid arclength-uniform points from every polygonal convex curve, identifies a shape-invariant cubic exponent, a nontrivial sharp convex angle functional, the full equality class, and a regular-family scaling limit. Exact finite-interval equality for all polygons is more informative than a leading numerical asymptotic; the sampling model is a natural local nonsmooth analogue of classical random-triangle laws. The value is independent of unproved applications or formal certification.
